case_title: KRISHIKA LULLA & ORS. v. SHYAM VITHALRAO DEVKATIA&ANR.
statutory_provisions: Copyright Act s.63; IPC s.406, s.420
neutral_facts: The accused, who were involved in a film production, faced a criminal complaint alleging infringement of copyright in the title of a story synopsis. The complainant claimed that the title 'Desi Boys' was used by the accused for their film titled 'Desi Boyz', which was released in 2011. The complainant alleged that the title was the soul of his story and that its use by the accused constituted infringement. The accused argued that the title was not a literary work and therefore not protected by copyright. The case involved a dispute over whether the title of a story could be considered a literary work under copyright law. The accused sought to quash the criminal proceedings, which were dismissed by the trial court. The High Court also dismissed the applications to quash the complaint, stating that the facts would be determined at trial. The Supreme Court ultimately held that no copyright subsisted in the title of the story synopsis and that the criminal complaint was untenable.
